newsitem.title: GERMANY: D.Babcock unit sees profit fall in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: D.Babcock unit sees profit fall in 1996/97.

text.p: BDAG Balcke-Duerr AG, a unit of Germany's troubled engineering group Deutsche Babcock AG, said on Monday restructuring costs would push 1996/97 net income "clearly below" the 25 million marks ($15.2 million) it earned in the previous business year.

The plant construction unit expected revenue to rise 5.5 percent to 1.9 billion marks in the fiscal 1996/97 year, which ends September 30, chief executive Hans-Wolfgang Koch said at a news conference.
New orders in the first quarter of the current year rose 55 percent to 730 million marks, although new orders would dip 4.5 percent to 2.1 billion marks for the year, he added.
In 1995/96, Balcke-Duerr's sales fell 5.5 percent to 1.8 billion marks, while operating profit dropped 21 percent to 38 million marks. Its net profit total of 25 million marks was down 24 percent.
The company planned to cut its 1995/96 dividend to 15 marks per share from 18 marks per share.

The company's parent, Deutsche Babcock, this week ousted group chief executive Heyo Schmiedeknecht and appointed Klaus Lederer, the 48-year old head of ITT Automotive Europe, a unit of ITT Industries Inc., to replace him.
Schmiedeknecht resigned under pressure after the company slid to a 434 million mark net loss for 1995/96 after a 46 million mark net profit the year before.
-- Neal Boudette, Bonn Newsroom, +49-228 26097150 ($ = 1.642 German Marks)
